subject: Science
title: Science Exam 1
topic: Health & Lifestyle · Periodic Table · Motion & Pressure
intro: Write in full sentences for the longer questions. Use the number of marks as a guide to how many points to make.

questions.q: Which nutrient is mainly used for growth and repair of cells?
questions.ms: Protein

questions.q: A student adds Benedict's solution to a food sample and heats it. Sugar is present. What colour change do they see?
questions.ms: Blue to brick-red (or orange-red).

questions.q: Describe how to test a food sample for protein. Include the result you would see if protein is present.
questions.ms: 1 add Biuret solution (or copper sulfate then sodium hydroxide) to the food in solution; 1 blue at the start; 1 turns purple/lilac if protein present.

questions.q: A 13-year-old who trains for swimming every day needs more energy from food than a 13-year-old who does little exercise. Explain why.
questions.ms: 1 more physical activity / more muscle movement; 1 respiration releases more energy, so more energy (kJ) is needed from food. Also accept growth if linked.

questions.q: Name the enzyme that breaks down fats (lipids). Name the products it makes.
questions.ms: 1 lipase; 1 fatty acids and glycerol.

questions.q: Describe what happens to food in the small intestine.
questions.ms: Any 3: enzymes finish digestion; large molecules broken into small soluble molecules; small molecules absorbed into the blood; villi give a large surface area; thin walls / good blood supply.

questions.q: Explain one way that smoking tobacco harms the body.
questions.ms: 1 named harmful substance (tar / nicotine / carbon monoxide); 1 linked effect: tar damages cilia or causes cancer, CO reduces oxygen carried by blood, nicotine is addictive / raises heart rate.

questions.q: Which element is in Group 1 and Period 3 of the Periodic Table?
questions.ms: Sodium

questions.q: Element X is shiny, conducts electricity and has a high melting point. Its oxide is basic. What is X most likely to be?
questions.ms: A metal

Use the table to predict the melting point of rubidium.
questions.ms: 39 °C (melting point decreases down the group, by a smaller amount each time).

questions.q: Describe how the reactivity of Group 1 metals changes as you go down the group. Give an example of a reaction that shows this.
questions.ms: 1 more reactive going down; 1 example: potassium reacts more violently with water than sodium/lithium (fizzes, lilac flame, moves faster).

questions.q: Explain why the elements in Group 0 (the noble gases) are very unreactive.
questions.ms: 1 full outer shell of electrons; 1 so they do not need to gain, lose or share electrons (stable).

questions.q: Chlorine gas is bubbled into potassium bromide solution. Predict what you would see and explain why it happens.
questions.ms: 1 solution turns orange/brown; 1 bromine is displaced (potassium chloride + bromine formed); 1 because chlorine is more reactive than bromine (higher in Group 7).

questions.q: A car travels 150 km in 2.5 hours. Calculate its average speed in km/h.
questions.ms: 60 km/h. M1 speed = distance ÷ time, A1 150 ÷ 2.5 = 60.

questions.q: Explain the difference between average speed and instantaneous speed.
questions.ms: 1 average = total distance ÷ total time for the whole journey; 1 instantaneous = speed at one particular moment (e.g. speedometer reading).

questions.q: Car A drives at 70 km/h. Car B drives at 50 km/h in the same direction. What is the speed of car A relative to car B, in km/h?
questions.ms: 20 km/h

questions.q: Use the graph to work out the cyclist's speed in the first 2 seconds, in m/s.
A box weighs 600 N. Its base measures 0.5 m by 0.4 m. Calculate the pressure the box puts on the floor, in Pa.
questions.ms: 3000 Pa. M1 area = 0.5 × 0.4 = 0.2 m², M1 pressure = force ÷ area, A1 600 ÷ 0.2 = 3000 Pa.

questions.q: Explain why wearing snowshoes stops a person sinking into deep snow.
questions.ms: 1 snowshoes have a larger surface area; 1 same weight (force) spread over a larger area gives lower pressure.

questions.q: Explain why atmospheric pressure is lower at the top of a mountain than at sea level.
questions.ms: 1 less air above you / smaller weight of air pushing down; 1 air is less dense (fewer particles colliding) higher up.

questions.q: A force of 40 N is applied to a spanner, 0.25 m from the pivot. Calculate the moment of the force in N m.
questions.ms: 10 N m. M1 moment = force × distance from pivot, A1 40 × 0.25 = 10.

questions.q: Mia investigates how the height of a ramp affects the speed of a toy car at the bottom. Name the independent variable, the dependent variable and one control variable.
questions.ms: 1 IV height of ramp; 1 DV speed of the car; 1 control: same car / same mass / same surface / same length of ramp / same release method.

questions.q: Mia times the car three times: 2.4 s, 2.6 s and 2.5 s. Calculate the mean time in seconds.
